title: Trump Rejects Iran Counter-Proposal as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' — Tehran Demands Hormuz Sovereignty Recognition, War Reparations, Frozen Asset Release — Day 72
detail: The central diplomatic rupture of May 10, 2026 (Day 72): Iran delivered its formal counter-proposal to the US 14-point MOU framework, and Trump immediately rejected it on Truth Social with an all-caps post: 'I don't like it — TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!' Iran's counter-demands included: (1) formal US recognition of Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz; (2) compensation for war damages and reparations; (3) release of all frozen Iranian assets held in foreign banks; (4) an end to all fighting on all fronts, including Lebanon; (5) lifting of US oil sanctions and the naval blockade; and (6) cessation of what Tehran characterized as 'maritime piracy' against Iranian ships. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Nasser Kanani defended the counter-proposal as 'reasonable and generous,' arguing that no sovereign state could accept the US's 14-point maximalist framework without modifications. The fundamental gap between the two sides remains wide: the US demanded a 12–15 year enrichment moratorium; Iran offered approximately 5 years and refused to dismantle its enrichment program entirely. The US also refused any recognition of Iranian sovereignty over the strait, and Rubio had explicitly stated weeks earlier that Washington 'cannot accept paying a toll or coordinating with Iran' for Hormuz passage. Pakistan, serving as mediator, acknowledged the counter-proposal was a significant setback but said talks would continue. Market reaction was immediate: Brent crude spiked on the diplomatic rupture.

media.caption: Day 72: Trump rejects Iran's formal counter-proposal to the US MOU framework as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' — Tehran demands Hormuz sovereignty recognition, reparations, and frozen asset release

title: Lebanon: 51 Killed Including 2 Medics in Israeli Strikes in 24 Hours — Health Ministry Strikes on Medical Facilities in Bint Jbeil — Day 72
detail: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported 51 people killed in Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon in the 24-hour period through May 10, 2026 (Day 72), including two medical workers. Israeli strikes directly hit Lebanese Health Authority facilities in Qalawiya and Tibnin in the Bint Jbeil district, which human rights organizations condemned as a violation of international humanitarian law. The broader Lebanon toll since the conflict began in early March stood at 2,846 killed by May 10. The strikes occurred as the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire continued to fray ahead of its May 17 expiry date. Israel's operation in southern Lebanon was described as targeting Hezbollah infrastructure, with the IDF claiming prior warnings were issued. Lebanon's government called for an emergency UN Security Council session. Al Jazeera's May 11 live blog listed 'Israel kills 2 medics in Lebanon' as one of the day's top headlines.

media.caption: Day 72: Lebanon Health Ministry reports 51 killed including 2 medics in 24 hours of Israeli strikes — strikes hit health facilities in Bint Jbeil district
